To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of evolutionary information in the form of correlated mutations, in addition to the information contained in the sequence and secondary structure, improves the accuracy of contact map predictions, that the use of neural networks to predict protein contact maps improves the accuracy of predictions with respect to the use of only correlated mutations and that the combination of neural networks and correlated mutation improves the accuracy of the predictions with respect to either of these two methods alone.
the combination of correlated mutations and neural networks is a powerful tool for the prediction of protein contact maps.
neural network methods are able to predict protein contact maps, with accuracies of 0.20-0.25, and that these predictions are improved when using correlated mutation information.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new computational methods for protein folding, which are based on neural networks and on the analysis of correlated mutations.
the development of a method for predicting protein contact map with a high accuracy, based on neural network-based techniques and correlated mutations.
the development of a new method for the prediction of protein contact maps that exploits the information contained in evolutionary data, correlated mutations and secondary structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neural network method, when used in combination with the coordination number filter, is the best method to date for predicting protein contact map.
the method is a good predictor of contact maps of proteins.
the neural network approach is a powerful tool to predict the protein contact map.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the neural networks are trained to recognize the association rules between covalent structure and contact map, and then they are able to predict contact maps for new proteins, provided that the proteins are not homologous with the training data set.
the combination of evolutionary and correlated mutations information, together with a neural network approach, can be successfully applied to predict protein contacts.
neural networks can be trained to learn the complex relationship between the covalence of the protein structure and the contact map with high accuracy, provided the input is appropriately coded.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of evolutionary information and the combination of different predictors are crucial to obtain accurate contact maps.
the use of correlated mutations and evolutionary information can improve the performance of the prediction of protein contacts.
neural networks can be trained with a limited number of examples, provided that the examples are carefully selected and the training set is augmented with evolutionary and structural information.
